name: MongoDB.local Toronto
audience: developers, architects, IT professionals, DevOps engineers
description: A one-day MongoDB developer conference bringing the MongoDB.local series to Toronto, with technical sessions on modern application development, scaling in the AI era and hands-on access to MongoDB engineers. The full-day pass is $100 CAD including food and beverages.

name: Product-Led Summit Toronto
audience: product managers, product leaders, growth and SaaS professionals
description: The Toronto edition of Product-Led Alliance's global Product-Led Summit series, a two-day gathering of product leaders sharing how to build and scale product-led growth motions. Runs alongside sister editions in San Francisco, Boston, Chicago, Denver and Seattle.

name: Difinity Conference Toronto
audience: data engineers, BI developers, analytics professionals, data architects
description: The Toronto edition of Difinity, the Microsoft Fabric, Power BI and Data & AI conference that began in New Zealand in 2017 and has since expanded to Canada. Multi-track sessions plus a pre-conference day cover Fabric, Power BI, data engineering, governance and modern analytics platforms, hosted at the Microsoft Toronto office.

name: apidays Toronto
audience: API developers, architects, platform leaders, engineering decision-makers
description: The Toronto stop of the global apidays conference series, themed The Execution Layer: Building APIs for the Agentic Era, with 100+ sessions on API design, security, monetization and agent-ready platforms. Co-located with GenerationAI Toronto and Green IO Toronto.

name: BSides Toronto
venue: Ted Rogers School of Management, Toronto Metropolitan University, 55 Dundas St W
description: Toronto's community-run Security BSides conference, a grassroots two-day event of information security talks hosted at Toronto Metropolitan University. An open call for papers and low-cost tickets keep it accessible to students and newcomers.

name: BSides Montreal
venue: Bibliotheque et Archives nationales du Quebec (BAnQ), 475 Boul. de Maisonneuve E
audience: security professionals, newcomers to infosec, students
description: Montreal's Security BSides, a deliberately intimate single-day infosec conference where talks are not recorded or published online so speakers and attendees can talk openly. Mixes conference sessions with poster presentations and hallway conversation.

name: GoSec
audience: cybersecurity professionals, practitioners, researchers, security leaders
description: A long-running Montreal cybersecurity conference with six keynotes, hands-on workshops and 40+ sessions from international experts and practitioners. Attendance is offered both in person and virtually.

name: PGConf.dev
audience: postgresql developers, contributors, community organizers, advanced users
description: The PostgreSQL Development Conference, aimed at contributors and community rather than end-user training: keynotes, technical sessions, an in-person commitfest and a closing attendee-driven unconference day. The 2026 edition ran May 19-22 at SFU Harbour Centre in Vancouver; 2027 moves to Montreal.

name: seL4 Summit
audience: seL4 developers, users, researchers, embedded and high-assurance systems engineers
description: The annual summit of the seL4 Foundation, covering the formally verified seL4 microkernel and the tools, products and projects built on it. The 2026 Vancouver edition opens with a full day on real-world applications of formally verified software, followed by two days of technical content.

name: YYC DataCon
audience: data practitioners, technical leads, analytics and data decision-makers
description: Western Canada's community-led data conference, themed From Insight to Impact: Doing Data Right, with 30+ speakers on production data systems, applied LLMs, data platforms, governance and privacy. Tickets run from $89 general to $299 executive.

name: BSides Vancouver Island
description: Vancouver Island's Security BSides conference, a community-organized day of information security talks at the Victoria Conference Centre with an open call for presenters. Tickets are sold through Eventbrite.

name: BSides Saskatoon
audience: security professionals, students, hackers, curious newcomers
description: Security BSides Saskatoon (BSidesYXE), a grassroots single-day infosec conference in its third year, covering threat detection, offensive and defensive security, critical infrastructure and OT security, and AI-assisted detection. Built to grow the local security community outside the mainstream conference circuit.

name: BSides Halifax
venue: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
audience: security professionals, students, newcomers to infosec
description: Halifax's Security BSides, a community infosec conference held at Dalhousie's Faculty of Computer Science for experts, students and the merely curious. The 2025 edition sold out, with talks on threat exposure management, nation-state attacks, LoRa-based decentralized communications and secure system design.

name: BarCamp Philly
venue: Huntsman Hall, The Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania
description: Philadelphia's longest-running unconference: attendees propose talks in the morning, vote on the ones they want, and the day's schedule is built on the spot across six session blocks from 8am to 5pm.

name: Startup Grind Global Conference
description: Startup Grind's flagship Silicon Valley gathering built around AI, startups and fundraising, with 175+ sessions, 150+ exhibiting startups and 1,000+ investors scouting deals over two days.

name: MongoDB.local NYC
description: A full-day MongoDB technical event on taking AI from demos to production, covering architectural patterns for agentic systems, memory and retrieval workloads, live product announcements and 1:1 expert office hours.

name: MongoDB.local Dallas
audience: developers, architects, IT professionals, DevOps engineers
description: The Dallas-Fort Worth stop on MongoDB's .local tour, a one-day event of technical sessions and expert guidance on building and scaling modern applications for the AI era.

name: Stripe Sessions
audience: developers, business leaders, payments and platform teams
description: Stripe's annual user conference on the economic infrastructure for AI, with product keynotes and breakout tracks on agentic commerce, payments, revenue optimization, platform economics, risk and stablecoins.

name: Atlassian Team
audience: engineering and IT teams, team leaders, Atlassian customers
description: Atlassian's global conference for AI-forward teamwork, mixing keynotes and product announcements with hands-on sessions on human plus AI collaboration across Jira, Confluence and the wider Atlassian platform. A digital pass streams the event for remote attendees.

name: MLconf
audience: data scientists, ML engineers, researchers, technical leaders
description: A single-track machine learning conference where practitioners from major tech companies and enterprises present ML algorithms, platforms, tooling, best practices and lessons learned from production systems.

name: NY SMART I-Corridor Semiconductor Summit
audience: semiconductor industry leaders, manufacturers, suppliers, workforce and economic development professionals
description: A two-day summit run by the NY SMART I-Corridor tech hub coalition to strengthen Upstate New York's semiconductor supply chain, workforce pipeline and innovation ecosystem.

name: CHM Live
description: The Computer History Museum's flagship live event series of original productions, interviews and panels exploring historical and current issues in technology, entrepreneurship and innovation. The next production, The Silicon Gold Rush, runs 27 August 2026.

name: Hacker Dojo Events
description: Hacker Dojo is a Mountain View community hackerspace running near-daily talks, workshops, study groups, DevHouses, demo nights and hackathons. Over 20,000 members and 135+ events on the calendar at any time; most sessions are free to attend.

name: Veteran Innovation Hackathon
description: A three-day build weekend at Hacker Dojo where veterans, engineers, designers and nonprofit leaders prototype solutions to the barriers veterans face accessing support services. Day one is veteran storytelling and team formation, day three is demos and judging.

name: AI in Education Summit
venue: Khan Lab School Middle & Upper School, 1200 Villa Street
description: A one-day summit hosted by Khan Lab School on how AI is changing teaching and learning, with talks and hands-on workshops from speakers including Sal Khan, Isabelle Hau and Alex Kotran. Free to attend.

name: BayPIGgies (Bay Area Python Interest Group)
description: The Bay Area Python Interest Group, formed in 1999 and part of the Python Software Foundation Meetup Pro network. Meets the fourth Thursday of every other month for lightning talks and technical presentations; free to attend.

name: ROS By-The-Bay
description: The Bay Area meetup for Robot Operating System users, run with Open Robotics. Monthly evening talks on ROS, Gazebo and the wider robotics ecosystem, frequently hosted at the Bosch USA headquarters in Sunnyvale; recent nights drew 89-121 attendees.

name: The Montgomery Summit
description: An invitation-only Santa Monica technology summit presented by March Capital that gathers 1,200+ entrepreneurs, investors and executives for 100+ company presentations, fireside chats and one-on-one meetings.

name: Santa Monica New Tech
venue: Rotating Santa Monica coffee shops and online
description: A Silicon Beach community of startup founders, builders and curious minds exploring AI, blockchain and quantum computing. Its core recurring format is the free Sunday morning Open Coffee Club, alongside occasional demo and speaker nights.

name: ITEXPO
audience: IT professionals, MSPs, channel partners, service providers, developers
description: A three-day business technology event at the Broward County Convention Center with 150+ breakout sessions, 300+ exhibitors and ten collocated events spanning AI, cloud, cybersecurity and communications. Draws over 7,000 attendees, mostly channel partners and service providers.

name: Ocean Exchange
audience: founders, investors, ocean and sustainability innovators
description: An annual innovation competition and gathering for the sustainable blue economy, where shortlisted startups and university teams pitch for Neptune and Collegiate Awards worth $100,000 each. Categories span alternative materials, energy, digitalization, fisheries and water treatment.

name: InsurTech America Symposium
description: InsurTech Hartford's flagship two-day conference, now positioned as a national gathering, with keynotes, breakout tracks, a startup showcase, the Making Waves Awards and the EmpowerHER programme for women leaders in insurance. The 2026 edition ran 13-14 April at the Connecticut Convention Center.

name: InsurTech Hartford Connect & Protect
audience: insurance and insurtech professionals, risk and cyber leaders
description: A one-day InsurTech Hartford event bringing carriers, brokers and startups together around connected risk and protection technology, held the same day as the Innovation Challenge Awards.

name: InsurTech Hartford Innovation Challenge Awards
description: The awards evening for InsurTech Hartford's annual Innovation Challenge, where shortlisted insurtech startups present to carriers and investors and the winners are announced.

name: Connecticut Digital Government Summit
audience: state and local government IT leaders and public-sector technologists
description: A one-day Government Technology summit for Connecticut state and municipal technology leaders covering cybersecurity, AI, data governance and digital service delivery. Free to public-sector attendees.

name: Rochester Security Summit
venue: Joseph A. Floreano Rochester Riverside Convention Center
audience: security professionals, IT staff, government and law enforcement
description: A two-day regional information security conference running since 2006, with multiple talk tracks, 40+ exhibitors, a capture-the-flag competition and a lockpick village. CPE credits available; two-day passes from $280 early bird.

name: Imagine RIT: Creativity and Innovation Festival
venue: Rochester Institute of Technology campus, 30 Lomb Memorial Drive
description: RIT's campus-wide innovation festival with more than 400 interactive student exhibits and roughly 3,100 exhibitors across engineering, computing, imaging science and design. Free and open to the public, 10am to 5pm.

name: BrickHack
venue: RIT SHED, Rochester Institute of Technology
description: RIT's 24-hour student invention marathon where teams build apps, websites, games and interactive media with mentors from sponsoring tech companies. Free and open to any enrolled university student aged 18+, with prize pools over $3,600.

name: 5 Across Pitch Competition
venue: The Mane on Main, 201 E Main St (venues rotate)
audience: founders, investors, students, local business community
description: Awesome Inc's long-running monthly pitch night where five local startups pitch for a $500 prize, with networking and dinner beforehand and a December finals night at the Kentucky Theatre.

name: Awesome Fellowship Demo Day
description: The closing showcase for each cohort of the Awesome Fellowship accelerator, where Kentucky founders present their companies over lunch at Awesome Inc's downtown Lexington hub. Powered by Chase.

name: Kentucky Entrepreneur Hall of Fame Induction
venue: Central Bank Center, 430 W Vine St
audience: founders, investors, business and tech community
description: An annual celebration dinner run out of Awesome Inc that inducts Kentucky's most notable entrepreneurs, including technology company founders, into the state's Entrepreneur Hall of Fame.

name: Cultivator Community Night
audience: founders, students, investors, Saskatchewan tech community
description: An open community night hosted by Cultivator powered by Conexus, showcasing big ideas, bold founders and Saskatchewan innovation with short talks and open networking.

name: 24 Hour Startup: AGTECH
description: Cultivator's 24-hour build sprint run on the floor of Canadian Western Agribition, where teams go from raw idea to pitched agtech startup in a single day.

name: Cultivator Startup Summit
description: Cultivator's annual founder-focused summit in Regina, built around founder stories, practical scaling sessions and connections between Saskatchewan startups and investors.

name: Cultivator STARTup Showcase
description: Demo day for each cohort of Cultivator's START program, where early-stage Saskatchewan founders pitch their companies at Cultivator HQ in Regina.

name: Jersey City Entrepreneurs: The Venture Garden
venue: Rotating Jersey City cafes (Canard Cafe Bar, O Kafe Hamilton Park, Ko Cafe)
description: A biweekly-to-weekly Jersey City gathering for founders, creators and operators, run as small Venture Garden sessions with introductions, group discussion of live business problems and open networking.

name: tech SAVannah Tech Tuesday
description: The monthly no-agenda happy hour of tech SAVannah, the city's 900-member community for coders, designers and founders, held at Hop Atomica alongside occasional special events such as the Explorers and Builders Guild.

name: BSides Idaho Falls
venue: Idaho State University Idaho Falls Campus, 1784 Science Center Dr
audience: information security professionals, IT staff, students
description: An all-volunteer Security BSides conference for eastern Idaho, organised by the Eastern Idaho Cybersecurity Educational Alliance, with talks and networking on the ISU Idaho Falls campus. The CFP for the 2027 edition closes in December 2026.

name: University of Idaho Engineering Design EXPO
audience: students, industry partners, recruiters, K-12 and community
description: The longest-running student engineering and technology innovation showcase in the Pacific Northwest, where University of Idaho capstone teams demo industry-sponsored projects to judges, recruiters and the public. More than 500 students take part each year.

name: Code & Supply
description: Pittsburgh's largest software-professional community, running free lectures and social nights alongside paid deep-dive workshops, plus livestreamed coding sessions and a job board. Founded in 2013 and organised through its Meetup group.

name: BSides Pittsburgh
description: A one-day community security conference at Rivers Casino running 8am to 5pm with an after-party, part of the global Security BSides network. Talks span offensive and defensive security for Pittsburgh-area infosec professionals.

name: AlphaLab Demo Day
description: The public showcase closing each AlphaLab accelerator cohort, where Pittsburgh software, hardware, robotics and life-sciences founders pitch after six months of customer discovery and mentorship. The 2026 cohort event drew over 300 investors, mentors and community members.

name: CyberBay Summit
audience: cybersecurity practitioners, researchers, CISOs, government and academic leaders
description: Tampa Bay's cybersecurity and AI summit, powered by the University of South Florida, bringing government, academia and industry together across five tracks including AI and cyber innovation, CISO leadership, practitioner tooling and workforce development.

name: Tampa Bay Wave BlueTech|X Pitch Night
description: Pitch night closing Tampa Bay Wave's BlueTech accelerator cohort, where ocean- and water-technology startups present to investors and the Tampa innovation community. One of Wave's sector pitch-night series alongside CyberTech|X and HealthTech|X.

name: Tampa Bay Wave Hall of Fame Awards
audience: tech and business leaders, founders, investors
description: An evening awards celebration honouring the innovators who shaped Tampa Bay's startup ecosystem, doubling as Tampa Bay Wave's annual fundraiser. Held on the Florida Aquarium rooftop for the region's tech and business leadership.

name: SouthEast LinuxFest
audience: linux users, sysadmins, open source developers, hobbyists
description: A free community-run Linux and open-source conference billed as Linux in the GNU/South, with talks and workshops on ZFS, self-built routers, sensor networks, open-source AI agents, amateur radio and retro gaming, plus LAN parties and a swapfest. Remote streaming access costs $5.

name: Open Source 101 Charlotte
description: A one-day introductory-to-intermediate conference on the processes and tools foundational to open source, open tech and the open web, run in downtown Charlotte by the All Things Open network. Offered both in person and live-streamed.

name: DevFest Charlotte
description: The annual free developer conference run by Google Developer Group Charlotte (1,100+ members) at UNC Charlotte, with sessions on AI, Go concurrency and next-generation cloud security. Supported by UNC Charlotte's business school and School of Data Science.

name: Buffalo Game Space Game Development Meeting
description: The monthly in-person gathering of Buffalo Game Space, a 501(c)(3) makerspace for game creators, where members discuss development techniques and show works in progress. Paired with a virtual project night and a virtual game developer hangout for the group's 1,290 members.

name: 9D Jam
description: Buffalo Game Space's relaxed nine-day summer game jam, framed as spending nine days in the middle of summer leisurely making a game. Run virtually so participants can pace themselves rather than sprint a weekend.

name: 43North Speaker Series
description: 43North's rolling calendar of Buffalo founder events: fireside chats with portfolio CEOs, Fly In A VC investor sessions, live product and CRM walkthroughs, and go-to-market talks. Free and open to the regional startup community.

name: RIHub Pizza & Pitches
description: A recurring informal pitch night at RIHub where Southern New England founders present to peers and mentors over pizza and get live feedback. Runs alongside RIHub's Open Coffee and New England Female Founders programming.

name: GDG Providence
description: A 600-member Google Developer Group chapter for people building with Google technology in Rhode Island, running monthly sessions of practical demos and discussion built on Google Cloud. Mostly virtual with occasional in-person meetups in Providence.

name: MIT Bitcoin Expo
audience: bitcoin developers, cryptographers, researchers, policy makers
description: The MIT Bitcoin Club's annual two-day expo on MIT's campus, with keynotes, technical talks on Layer 2 and quantum resistance, a workshop and a hackathon component. The 2026 edition, themed Freedom for All, featured 25+ speakers including Bitcoin Core contributors and an SEC commissioner.

name: MIT $100K Entrepreneurship Competition
venue: MIT Sloan School of Management and MIT Media Lab
description: A student-run competition since 1990 that runs three contests from September to May: Pitch (90-second pitches, $5K), Accelerate (prototypes, $10K, live finals at the MIT Media Lab) and Launch ($100K grand prize), awarding over $300K in non-dilutive funding a year. Past finalists include HubSpot, Akamai and Harmonix.

name: Cambridge Science Festival
audience: families, students, general public, science communicators
description: A STEAM festival running since 2007, anchored by the Cambridge Science Carnival on the Kendall/MIT Open Space with 100+ activity booths, demonstrations, live music, installations and the popular Robot Petting Zoo. The format is being reimagined for 2026.

name: NYC Resistor Craft Night
description: The regular open night at NYC Resistor, a hacker collective and shared space in Park Slope, Brooklyn, where the public can use laser cutters and other shop equipment and work alongside members. The space also runs Synthesizer Night, Repair Cafes and classes in soldering, soft circuits and casting.

name: Genspace Community Biology Programs
audience: adults, high-school and university students, artists, aspiring biotech professionals
description: The world's first community biology lab, open in Brooklyn since 2009, running hands-on classes taught by instructors from top NYC institutions plus public programs, the Biorocket high-school internship, the Break Into Biotech career track and an artist-in-residence programme.

name: GDG Brooklyn AI Fashion Hackathon
audience: developers, designers, beginners with no coding experience required
description: Runway to Reality, an AI fashion hackathon from the 1,500-member Google Developer Group Brooklyn, open to all skill levels with no coding experience required. Part of the chapter's AI Learning Labs and Builder Days series, sponsored by Vonage, General Assembly and Google Cloud.

name: Hack Midwest
audience: software engineers and designers of any skill level
description: A free 24-hour app-building competition in downtown Kansas City drawing 350+ engineers and designers, with $10,000 in cash prizes and trophies. Three meals are provided and organisers match solo participants into teams.

name: SecKC
description: Kansas City's longest-running monthly security meetup, a community of hackers, makers, builders and breakers with talks each month plus an active Discord. The September 2026 session covers network sniffing and the origins of Wireshark.

name: DevFest KC
description: The annual one-day developer conference from Google Developer Group Kansas City (487 members), with sessions on AI tooling, Android and spec-driven development. Speakers are selected through an open Sessionize call.

name: a2Tech360
audience: entrepreneurs, researchers, investors, job seekers, general public
description: Ann Arbor SPARK's eleven-day celebration of the region's technology ecosystem, with eight signature events plus 20+ partner events covering entrepreneurship, pitch competitions, women in tech, life sciences, mobility and career development. Many sessions are free.

name: Tech Homecoming
audience: tech job seekers, recent graduates, experienced professionals
description: Ann Arbor SPARK's evening hiring mixer connecting top local tech companies with job seekers, from new graduates to experienced engineers. Free for job seekers, with free headshots, door prizes, food and drinks.

name: GDG Ann Arbor
description: A 615-member Google Developer Group chapter running Build with AI workshops and technical meetups through the year, and co-hosting Michigan DevFest with the Detroit, Toledo and Windsor chapters. Most local sessions are free.

name: CodeStock
audience: developers, engineers, IT professionals, technology leaders
description: East Tennessee's flagship two-day developer conference, drawing more than 600 developers, engineers and technology leaders from across the Southeast for community-sourced sessions. Attendees rate it 4.5/5, and super-early-bird tickets open well ahead of the event.

name: Knox Game Jam
description: Knox Game Design's annual 48-hour game jam, open to any engine or library, where teams build a game to a surprise theme; the most recent edition ran on Limited Resources. Entries compete for recognition and prizes rather than cash.

name: Knox Game Design
audience: game designers and developers of all skill levels
description: Knoxville's game-development group, running regular in-person meetings with member presentations on topics from retro console programming to modern engines, plus a long-running podcast. Open to beginners and professionals alike.

name: DevSpace Conference
description: Huntsville's polyglot developer conference at the Von Braun Center, welcoming talks across many languages alongside sessions on professional and interpersonal skills; recent keynotes covered neurodivergence in testing and privacy-focused distributed app frameworks. Tickets run $150 to $300 depending on how early you book.

name: HudsonAlpha Tech Challenge
venue: HudsonAlpha Institute for Biotechnology, 800 Hudson Way NW
audience: high school and college students, developers, scientists, professionals
description: A weekend biotech hackathon on the HudsonAlpha campus where teams of up to five tackle challenges in genomics security, disease surveillance and microscopy analysis for up to $5,000 in prizes. Registration is $10 including a shirt and swag, and no prior biotech or coding experience is required.

name: Space and Missile Defense Symposium
audience: defense and aerospace engineers, government and allied military leaders, contractors
description: The leading educational, professional-development and networking event for the space and missile defense community, drawing 9,000+ attendees, 300+ exhibitors and 100+ sessions to the Von Braun Center in Huntsville.

name: SLOSS.tech
venue: Lyric Theatre and downtown Birmingham venues
audience: founders, funders, developers, students, early-career professionals
description: TechBirmingham's three-day tech and innovation conference connecting 1,400+ technologists, founders and leaders across the South, with 90+ speakers, a developer track run with BASE, and a pitch competition carrying $100,000 in top prizes.

name: Birmingham Women in Technology
description: TechBirmingham's ongoing community for women in technology, running monthly socials and programming around the Birmingham metro alongside the organisation's Tech Equals workshops and Agile practitioner talks. Socials typically cost around $10.

name: Innovation Depot Founders Round Table
audience: startup founders resident at Innovation Depot
description: A recurring morning peer session for founders based at Innovation Depot, Birmingham's startup accelerator and coworking hub, alongside its Depot Workshops and Founder Story talks. Programming is for members of the Voltage and Boost accelerator communities.

name: Scenic City Summit
venue: Chattanooga Convention Center; workshops at Chattanooga Marriott Downtown
audience: tech professionals, builders, educators, engineering leaders
description: Chattanooga's flagship regional technology conference, now in its eleventh year, pairing a day of hands-on workshops with a full conference day of talks under the banner Real Tech, Real Talk, Real Connections. Organised in partnership with ChaTech.

name: Tennessee Quantum Hackathon
description: A quantum-computing hackathon hosted by CO.LAB in Chattanooga, drawing on the city's quantum infrastructure and partners including EPB and Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Applications are open to students and early-career builders.

name: ChaTech Tech Tuesdays
description: The Chattanooga Technology Council's recurring community meetup, part of a programme that also includes the Senior Tech Forum, ChaTech Women, Chattanooga Data Professionals and a digital marketing meetup serving the 16-county region.

name: TENWEST Festival
description: Multi-day entrepreneurship and creativity festival across downtown Tucson, presented by Startup Tucson and the University of Arizona McGuire Center for Entrepreneurship. Billed as the largest entrepreneurship festival in the Southwest, it bundles summits, showcases and the IdeaFunding pitch competition.

name: IdeaFunding
description: Arizona's longest-running pitch competition, run by Startup Tucson. Early-stage founders pitch across tech and creative/community tracks for more than $50,000 in non-dilutive awards, culminating in a main-stage showcase at the Rialto Theatre.

name: TechMentor & Cybersecurity Live! @ Microsoft HQ
audience: IT pros, sysadmins, architects, security practitioners
description: Week-long IT-pro and cybersecurity training conference held on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, combining TechMentor and Cybersecurity Live! under one registration with deep-dive sessions on Azure, Microsoft 365, ransomware resilience and AI-assisted operations.

name: Microsoft Reactor Redmond
description: Microsoft's free technical community space on the Redmond campus, running a near-continuous stream of hands-on workshops, AI and cloud skilling sessions, demos and community meetups. Around 24,000 members; the physical Reactor space is also lent to outside organizers.

name: Maker Faire Yukon
description: The Yukon edition of Maker Faire, a two-day showcase of maker projects, hardware hacking, robotics and hands-on build stations for the territory's maker community.

name: Yukon Innovation Week
description: Territory-wide innovation week organized around Meet, Make and Grow pillars, giving Yukon innovators, entrepreneurs and social enterprises a platform of talks, workshops and an Innovation Day. Also produces a podcast series with local innovators.

name: Yukonstruct Maker Academy
description: Yukonstruct's rolling calendar of hands-on Makespace classes and shop orientations in Whitehorse, from woodshop certification to cosplay fabrication and weekly Repair Cafe nights, plus entrepreneurship sessions from its Cospace side.

name: WEtech Alliance Community Events
description: The regional innovation centre for Windsor-Essex and Chatham-Kent publishes a continuously updated community calendar of tech and startup events, including Hackforge Linux install parties and maker nights, founder info sessions, Tech Talks and networking mixers.

name: CyberForce Competition
description: The U.S. Department of Energy's flagship attack/defend cyber-physical competition, run in person since 2016. Up to 100 collegiate blue teams defend simulated energy infrastructure against a live red team over two days.

name: SANS NetWars Tournament
description: Six-hour hands-on capture-the-flag tournaments run on the SANS Cyber Ranges and held in person alongside SANS training events. Variants include Core, Cyber Defense, DFIR, GRID, Healthcare and ICS NetWars; entry is free with a paid multi-day course.

name: CyberSci National Finals
description: Canada's national student cybersecurity competition. Six in-person regional CTFs (Montreal, Ottawa, Toronto, Calgary, Vancouver and Atlantic Canada) feed an in-person national final in Ottawa, from which teams are selected to represent Canada at the ECSC and ICC.

name: Global Game Jam - University of Montana
venue: McGill Hall Room 223, University of Montana
description: University of Montana's Global Game Jam site, running the full 48-hour jam in the campus Games Lab with a Discord channel for remote jammers. Open to students and the wider Missoula game-dev community.

name: Global Game Jam San Antonio
description: San Antonio's Global Game Jam site, hosted by the Greater Gaming Society at Shenanigans Gaming. Jammers build games on site over the jam week and present finished projects live on the society's Twitch stream.

name: Global Game Jam - College of Charleston
venue: Harbor Walk East, 2nd Floor Innovation Center
audience: students, local tech professionals, amateur game developers
description: College of Charleston's Global Game Jam site at the Harbor Walk East Innovation Center, open to students, Lowcountry tech professionals, amateur game devs and complete beginners for the weekend-long jam.

name: Global Game Jam Albuquerque
description: Albuquerque's Global Game Jam site hosted jointly by the University of New Mexico and the Albuquerque Game Developers Guild at Mesa Del Sol, with in-person jamming plus a Discord track and post-jam presentations.

name: TOJam
audience: coders, artists, musicians, game makers of all levels
description: The Toronto Game Jam, a free three-day in-person jam running since 2006 that has produced over 1,000 games with more than 7,000 participants. Held at George Brown College and open to makers at every skill level.

name: PodCamp Toronto
audience: digital creators, media and tech professionals, podcasters
description: Long-running Canadian unconference for digital media and technology creators, running roughly 60 attendee-driven sessions across eight streams over a weekend. Free general admission with optional paid networking tiers.

name: Minnedemo
description: Minnestar's showcase of working technology products built in Minnesota. Seven-minute live demos with no slides allowed - a geek show and tell staged at the Ordway in St. Paul.

name: CDL Super Session
venue: Rotman School of Management, University of Toronto
description: Creative Destruction Lab's annual invitation-only showcase of its graduating seed-stage science and technology companies, pairing founders with investors and scientists for focused feedback and matchmaking sessions at Rotman.

name: Berkeley SkyDeck Demo Day
description: Demo day for each cohort of UC Berkeley's SkyDeck accelerator, where roughly two dozen venture-scale startups pitch to an audience of investors and the Berkeley innovation community.

name: Mira Awards
description: TechPoint's annual gala celebrating Indiana's technology community, honouring companies, founders, educators and investors across a slate of categories. Moving to the Signia by Hilton in downtown Indianapolis for 2027.

name: Colorado Technology Association APEX Awards
audience: CEOs, CTOs, CISOs, entrepreneurs, public-sector technology leaders
description: Running since 2001, the APEX Awards combine a half-day summit with keynotes, panels and an Innovation Hall before a luncheon announcing winners in nine categories including Company of the Year and the Bob Newman Lifetime Achievement Award.

name: TAG Chairs' Gala
description: The Technology Association of Georgia's evening gala honouring leaders of the state's technology community, one of TAG's signature annual events alongside Fintech South and the Georgia Technology Summit.

name: San Francisco Python Meetup Group
description: Founded in 2008 and the largest community-run meetup in the Bay Area, with a presentation night on the second Wednesday of every month plus 20+ developer events a year. Also organizes the PyBay conference.

name: Boston Python User Group
audience: Python developers of all skill levels
description: One of the largest Python user groups in North America, running a monthly presentation night, monthly informal project nights, Python Over Coffee socials and online office hours. Free to attend.

name: Data Science DC
audience: data scientists, ML engineers, analysts, students
description: A program of the non-profit Data Community DC and one of the region's largest technical meetups, hosting roughly monthly talks on machine learning, AI tooling and data science practice.

name: Toronto JavaScript
description: Volunteer-run non-profit community of 13,000+ members running monthly in-person TechTalk nights in Toronto (typically 90-135 attendees) plus online sessions, a Slack workspace and a speaker pipeline for new presenters.

name: Puget Sound Programming Python (PuPPy)
description: The Puget Sound region's main Python community, with monthly talk nights plus separate project hack nights and socials at Seattle-area venues. Free to attend and part of the Python Software Foundation meetup network.

name: SeattleJS
description: Seattle's longest-running web and JavaScript meetup, running biweekly one-hour hackathon-plus-presentation nights and weekly code kata sessions in person and online.

name: PyLadies
audience: women and gender minorities in the Python community
description: International mentorship group with roughly 25 US chapters (Austin, Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Seattle, San Francisco and more) and Canadian chapters in Calgary, Montreal, Toronto and Vancouver, each running local in-person talks and coding workshops.

name: Georgia Tech All-Majors Career Fair
venue: Georgia Tech Exhibition Hall / Campus Recreation Center
audience: students and alumni across all majors, employer recruiters
description: Georgia Tech's premier recruiting event, held each fall and spring over two days. Hundreds of employers meet thousands of undergraduate and graduate candidates for co-op, internship and full-time technical roles.

name: Django Girls New York City
description: A Django Girls one-day beginner programming workshop in New York City, where participants build and deploy their first Django web application with one-on-one coach support. Django Girls workshops are free and volunteer-run.

name: The Carpentries Workshops
description: Two-day hands-on workshops in Software, Data and Library Carpentry, taught by certified volunteer instructors at universities and research institutions across North America. Learners code along with instructors; no prior experience required.

name: Hacker Dojo
description: Silicon Valley non-profit hackerspace running a continuous programme of community talks, workshops, hackathons and hardware-lab sessions, plus an AI Career Initiative and summer accelerator. Membership from $75/month, with many events open to the public.

name: Boston Festival of Indie Games
description: Boston's biggest indie games event, a one-day showfloor of digital and tabletop indie titles at the Cyclorama with the Figgie Awards showcase, developer booths and community programming.
